result.summary: The environment features wide sidewalks on both sides of a broad roadway, but lacks formal pedestrian crossing infrastructure at the visible junction. The street is characterized by a large institutional structure with a fenced perimeter on one side and residential properties on the other, creating a somewhat desolate pedestrian experience with long crossing distances.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: Pedestrians crossing at the junction have no designated space or priority, increasing the risk of conflict with turning vehicles.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The wide, open asphalt without traffic calming encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases pedestrian exposure time during crossings.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install ladder or zebra-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees on the left side to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide, paved sidewalk in a residential area, but it lacks basic safety infrastructure like marked crossings or buffers. The roadway is wide and curved, with vegetation that may obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked crossing points for pedestrians across the wide, curved roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions
hazards.description: Large trees and dense hedges on the inside of the curve may block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the road along the curve

hazards.name: Poor sidewalk maintenance
hazards.description: Significant weed growth in the sidewalk joints creates uneven surfaces and potential tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks to provide designated crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or manage hedges and trees to ensure clear sightlines are maintained around the curve.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features wide but poorly maintained sidewalks adjacent to a low-traffic roundabout. While the roundabout naturally slows vehicles, the lack of marked crossings and physical buffers between the walkway and the roadway reduces overall pedestrian safety and comfort.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the junction, forcing pedestrians to cross without a designated or protected space.
hazards.location_in_image: At the junction where the approach road meets the roundabout

hazards.name: Poor sidewalk maintenance
hazards.description: Significant weed growth and cracking in the sidewalk pavement create potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the foreground roadway

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: The wide sidewalks are directly adjacent to the travel lane without any buffer like a planting strip or parked cars.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the length of the visible roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental-style crosswalks at all legs of the junction to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Maintenance
interventions.description: Resurface the existing walkways to remove weeds and cracks, ensuring a smooth and accessible path for all users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to increase the physical and psychological distance from traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, continuous concrete sidewalk bordering an athletic field. While the walkway is unobstructed, it lacks a buffer from the roadway and features no street trees or pedestrian-scale lighting.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: There is no buffer zone, such as a planting strip or parked cars, between the sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Sidewalk debris and minor cracking
hazards.description: Litter and small cracks in the concrete surface present minor tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Install Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Adding a planting strip with street trees would provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lights to improve visibility and perceived safety for pedestrians using the walkway at night.
